Examples: human life imputed to the soul at birth; Adam's original sin imputed to the old sin nature at birth; divine blessing imputed to imputed divine righteousness at spiritual maturity.
judicial imputation An imputation that has only one factor: that which is imputed. There is no natural affinity or prepared home in the recipient. It is a sovereign judicial act of God. Examples: all personal sins imputed to Christ at the cross; divine righteousness imputed to the believer at salvation.
imputed divine righteousness δικαιοσύνη θεοῦ dikaiosynē theou — righteousness of God The perfect righteousness of God judicially imputed to the believer at the moment of faith in Christ. It is the home and target — the affinity — for the real imputation of divine blessing in time. It is not the believer's own righteousness but God's, credited to the believer's account.
justification δικαίωσις dikaiōsis — justification, vindication The resultant status of the believer upon receiving the judicial imputation of divine righteousness at salvation. Justification means qualified for blessing in time and eternity — a candidate for the positive side of divine grace. It is not a statement of personal moral history.
prosperity εἰρήνη eirēnē — peace, prosperity, well-being In Romans 8:6 the term rendered 'prosperity' encompasses the full range of divine blessing imputed to the mature believer: the objective of the believer's life in time, organized into six categories — spiritual blessings, temporal blessings, blessing by association, historical impact, dying blessing, and undeserved suffering.
maturity adjustment to the justice of God The progressive spiritual growth of the believer through sustained intake of Bible doctrine, culminating in cracking the maturity barrier and advancing to supergrace. At this point the imputed divine righteousness demands, and the justice of God executes, the real imputation of divine blessing in time.
supergrace / ultra-supergrace Stages of spiritual maturity beyond the maturity barrier. Supergrace A and supergrace B denote progressive levels of attainment; ultra-supergrace designates maximum spiritual maturity, exemplified in Scripture by figures such as Moses, David, Isaiah, Jeremiah, and Paul.
pivot The body of mature believers in a national entity whose maturity adjustment to the justice of God sustains divine blessing on the nation and preserves it under historical adversity. As the pivot grows, the nation is preserved; as it shrinks, the nation is subject to the cycles of divine discipline.
blessing by association The mechanism by which unbelievers and reversionistic believers receive temporal blessing through proximity to a mature believer. God may bless those in the periphery of the mature believer directly (God as the visible source) or indirectly (the mature believer as the visible instrument). Peripheries include: loved ones, business associates, professional colleagues, social circle, local congregation, geographic community, heirs, and congregation members under a mature pastor.
dying grace The fifth category of divine blessing: the physical death of the mature believer in supergrace. At the point of dying grace, the sting and fear of death are removed, and death becomes the greatest experience in the believer's earthly life — a permanent change of station from phase two (time) to phase three (eternity). Psalm 116:15: 'Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His godly ones.'
undeserved suffering The sixth category of divine blessing: suffering that is not divine discipline but is permitted by God for the mature believer. The mature believer has capacity for undeserved suffering and handles it with stability; God transforms it into blessing. Full treatment at Romans 8:18–30.
old sin nature (OSN) σάρξ sarx — flesh The sin capacity inherited at birth through the male genetic line. At birth, Adam's original sin is imputed to the old sin nature as its prepared home — a real imputation. The old sin nature rules physical life through spiritual death. Its thought pattern is the subject of the first clause of Romans 8:6.
logistical grace God's provision of everything necessary for the believer's physical existence during the period between salvation and spiritual maturity. Logistical grace includes necessities and many pleasant provisions, but these are distinct from the real imputation of divine blessing, which awaits the attainment of spiritual maturity.

Chapter Two Hundred Eighty-Three

Romans 8:6 — The Integrity of God as the Sole Basis of Divine Blessing; Judicial and Real Imputations; Job 5 and the Grace Pipeline

Romans 8:6 “For to set the mind on the flesh is death, but to set the mind on the Spirit is life and peace.” (ESV)

Corrected translation: Consequently, the thought pattern of the old sin nature is death, but the thought pattern of the Spirit is capacity for life and prosperity — that is, blessings from the justice of God.

Romans 8:6 continues to develop the governing principle of this section: the two opposing thought patterns — that of the old sin nature and that of the indwelling Spirit — lead to radically different outcomes in the believer's life. The verse introduces the concept of prosperity as a technical category: not merely comfort or material well-being, but blessing that flows from divine integrity through what the Protocol Plan of God designates as the grace pipeline. To illuminate this principle, the chapter draws on Job 5, which provides Old Testament confirmation that all blessing originates in the justice of God and cannot be obtained through human effort, religious observance, or merit of any kind.

I. Review of Imputation Structure: Real and Judicial

All divine blessing to the believer is delivered as a real imputation. A real imputation always consists of two factors: the thing being imputed and its antecedent home — a prepared target with affinity for what is received. Four real imputations establish the framework of human existence and divine provision.

The Four Real Imputations

First, human life is imputed to the soul. The soul is the divinely prepared target; human life is the content imputed to it. There is natural affinity between these two factors, and this is the real imputation that constitutes physical existence.

Second, Adam's original sin is imputed to the genetically formed old sin nature. Every member of the human race is born a facsimile of Adam after his fall. The affinity between Adam's original sin and the old sin nature makes this a real imputation executed by the justice of God at birth.

Third, eternal life is imputed to regeneration. At the moment of salvation, the justice of God imputes eternal life to its target — the regenerate human spirit. Affinity exists between eternal life and the regenerate spirit prepared by God.

Fourth — and most complex — divine blessing in time is imputed to the righteousness of God already resident in the believer. This fourth real imputation cannot occur directly. It requires two prior judicial imputations, and this is what makes it the crown and culmination of the entire system.

The Two Judicial Imputations Required for Blessing

A judicial imputation differs from a real imputation in that there is no antecedent affinity between the content imputed and its target. The content is assigned by a judicial act of God rather than by natural correspondence.

Judicial imputation number one: at the cross, all personal sins of the entire human race were imputed to Jesus Christ, and the justice of God judged them in Him. These sins had no antecedent home in the perfect God-Man — there was no affinity. This was a purely judicial act. The penalty was paid in full.

Judicial imputation number two: at the moment of salvation, the righteousness of God is imputed to the believing sinner. Divine righteousness has no antecedent home in the sinner — it is not his own by nature. Again, there is no affinity. This too is a purely judicial act.

Only after these two judicial imputations does the fourth real imputation become possible. Because the believer now possesses imputed divine righteousness as a permanent target, the justice of God — the other half of divine integrity — can impute blessing to that righteousness without any compromise of the divine character. The justice of God gives to the righteousness of God. God gives to God. No attribute is compromised.

II. The Grace Pipeline: Why Human Effort Cannot Produce Blessing

The mechanism of divine blessing is best understood as a closed pipeline. The justice of God stands at the giving end. The righteousness of God — already resident in the believer as an imputed possession — stands at the receiving end. The pipeline is encapsulated: nothing from the human side can enter it.

Righteousness demands righteousness; justice demands justice. What righteousness demands, justice must execute. This is expressed in the formula: the righteousness of God demands blessing at maturity, and the justice of God executes what the righteousness demands. The technical designation for this category of blessing is paragraph SG2 — blessing from the justice of God to the mature believer — with six sub-categories, the sixth of which is undeserved suffering as blessing.

No human activity can penetrate this encapsulating screen. Witnessing, prayer, attendance at worship, tithing, sacrifice, service, obedience to any command of Scripture apart from the perception of doctrine — none of these functions connects to the pipeline. This is not because these activities are illegitimate. Many of them are commanded. But a commanded action and a blessed action are not equivalent. A command is issued to be obeyed; the blessing that flows from the integrity of God is given entirely on God's initiative, according to God's plan, without reference to human merit or effort.

The sole activity that relates to the blessing pipeline is the consistent, sustained intake of Bible doctrine over time — the operation of the Grace Apparatus for Perception (GAP). When maximum doctrine has been accumulated in the soul and the edifice complex is constructed, the maturity barrier is cracked. At that threshold, the righteousness of God demands blessing from the justice of God, and the justice of God executes that demand. The believer neither earns nor deserves the blessing; it is imputed because the integrity of God gives to the integrity of God.

III. Logistical Grace Distinguished from Mature Blessing

Between salvation adjustment and maturity adjustment, the believer is sustained by logistical grace — the provision of everything necessary for physical existence and continued momentum toward maturity. Logistical grace includes food, shelter, clothing, transportation, health, relationships, and every resource needed to sustain the advance. These provisions may be pleasant, even remarkable, and they are genuine expressions of divine care.

They are not, however, blessing in the technical sense of paragraph SG2. The distinction is not one of pleasantness but of source and mechanism. Logistical grace is God's provision for the journey; mature blessing is the destination. Logistical grace supports and advances the believer toward maturity; mature blessing is imputed when maturity is reached. The believer who mistakes logistical grace for the full scope of divine blessing has not yet grasped the scale of what awaits him at the maturity barrier.

Furthermore, God has no favorites. No believer receives preferential treatment on the basis of personality, prominence, relationship, or spiritual history. If the justice of God were to favor one believer above another, the divine integrity would be compromised, and no believer could receive blessing at all. The impeccability of divine integrity is the very foundation of the believer's security. Every mature believer has equal access to the same grace pipeline, and every mature believer receives blessing appropriate to his own capacity — which God provides through the same doctrine that produces the maturity.

IV. Job 5: Old Testament Confirmation of the Grace Pipeline

Job 5 is introduced as an Old Testament witness to the principles developed in Romans 8:6. The chapter does not receive extended exegesis here but is surveyed to confirm that the integrity of God as the exclusive source of blessing is not a New Testament innovation — it is the consistent testimony of Scripture across all dispensations.

Job 5:1 — The Futility of Human Appeal

The rhetorical question of Job 5:1 — to which of the holy ones will you turn? — establishes that no creature of integrity, however admirable, can serve as an intermediary for divine blessing. The word rendered 'holy ones' refers to believers of genuine integrity. The point is not that such persons are unworthy of respect or incapable of service, but that the source of all blessing is the integrity of God, not the integrity of man. Turning to any human source for the relief of divine discipline or for the acceleration of divine blessing misunderstands the mechanism entirely.

This principle applies directly to prayer as a social activity. Prayer is not an aspirin for pain induced by divine discipline. When a believer is under the discipline of the justice of God, the discipline will continue until its purpose is accomplished. No volume of intercessory prayer from others alters that trajectory. The appropriate response is rebound — naming known sins to God (1 John 1:9), recovering the filling of the Spirit, and resuming the advance toward maturity. Prayer has a legitimate and extensive scope, but it is not a substitute for Bible doctrine resident in the soul, and it cannot override the justice of God in the administration of discipline.

Job 5:2 — Maladjustment and Self-Induced Misery

Verse 2 identifies the fool as one destroyed by complaining — the believer who is maladjusted to the justice of God and responds to adversity with grievance rather than with doctrine. Jealousy is identified as the mechanism of self-destruction for the maladjusted believer. Jealousy is a form of self-induced misery: the jealous believer compounds whatever pressure he is under by adding the corrosive effect of coveting what others possess. Conversely, the believer who is adjusted to the justice of God recognizes that what others have is irrelevant to his own relationship with divine integrity.

Job 5:3–5 — The Instability of Prosperity Without Capacity

The image of the fool taking root and his home decaying in a moment illustrates the fundamental principle that there are no advantages to the advantages without the advantage — that is, no benefit to prosperity without the capacity for it. Wealth, position, family security, and social prominence cannot produce happiness in a soul that lacks the doctrine-built capacity to receive them. The reversal described in verses 3–5 — the new home, the confiscated harvest, the son killed in battle — reflects the instability of a life built on logistical grace mistaken for permanent blessing.

Job 5:6–7 — The Source of Trouble

Evil does not come from the dust; trouble does not sprout from the ground. The source of trouble in human life is the old sin nature and the functioning of the ruler of this world within his domain. Man is born into trouble as surely as sparks fly upward. Only adjustment to the justice of God — beginning with salvation adjustment and progressing through maturity adjustment — can transform the believer's experience of adversity into a vehicle of blessing.

Job 5:8–11 — The Integrity of God as the Exclusive Source of Blessing

Job's own declaration in verse 8 introduces the paradigm of the mature believer: seeking God through the intake of doctrine and placing every cause — every instance of adversity, pressure, or testing — before the Godhead by means of the faith-rest technique. Faith-rest takes trouble off the believer and imposes it upon God, who can handle it. This is not resignation; it is the intelligent application of doctrine to circumstances.

Verse 9 describes the God who manufactures great and unsearchable things. The Hebrew participle is from the verb asah (עָשָָה), which denotes the making of something from existing materials. The existing material, in context, is the integrity of God itself. Divine blessing is manufactured out of the very substance of what God is — His righteousness and His justice — and is then imputed to the mature believer as a real imputation without compromise of any attribute.

Verse 11 — 'He sets the lowly in high places' — describes promotion as a real imputation from the justice of God to the righteousness of God. Promotion, like every other category of mature blessing, passes through the grace pipeline. It cannot be earned, leveraged, or accelerated by human effort. Verse 11 also introduces the principle that those who mourn are lifted to safety, anticipating the sixth category of paragraph SG2: undeserved suffering as a vehicle of blessing for the mature believer. The pipeline does not stop flowing because the believer is in suffering. Historical adversity — whether personal or national — does not interrupt the blessing that the justice of God sends to the righteousness of God in the soul of the mature believer.

Job 5:12–15 — The Craftiness of Enemies and the Deliverance of God

Verses 12–15 describe a consistent pattern: those who scheme against the believer with cleverness and cunning run into darkness rather than accomplishing their purpose. The believer is delivered from the sword of the mouth — slander, maligning, false judgment — by the integrity of God, not by his own defense or by the intervention of allies. The needy believer under the rule of a tyrant is delivered by divine integrity because his blessing is inside the pipeline, beyond the reach of any external power. No political arrangement, no dictatorial regime, no combination of historical circumstances can deprive the mature believer of what the justice of God has determined to give.

Job 5:17–18 — Divine Discipline and Rebound

Verse 17 introduces the principle that divine discipline, rightly received, is itself a form of blessing. The believer who is disciplined and responds with rebound rather than complaint does not lose momentum. He names his known sins to God, recovers the filling of the Spirit, and continues his advance toward maturity. Verse 18 — 'He wounds that He may bind; He bruises that His hand may heal' — encapsulates the purpose of rebound adjustment to the justice of God: the same divine integrity that administers the wound also provides the healing, and the healing is designed to restore and advance rather than merely to return to a neutral state.

Job 5:19 — Six Troubles: Introduction

The chapter concludes with the beginning of verse 19, which introduces the enumeration of six troubles from which the integrity of God delivers the mature believer. This verse stands as a gateway to the sixth category of paragraph SG2 — undeserved suffering as blessing — which will be developed fully in Romans 8:18–30. The parallel between the six troubles of Job 5 and the suffering-glory pattern of Romans 8 provides the Old Testament foundation for one of the most significant doctrinal passages in the epistle.

V. The Blessing Pipeline Applied to Historical Circumstances

The grace pipeline operates independently of historical conditions. Whether the national entity is in a period of prosperity — as Rome was during the Antonine Caesars — or in a period of severe historical adversity, the justice of God continues to send blessing down the pipeline to the righteousness of God in the soul of the mature believer. No external circumstance can interrupt that transmission.

At the national level, the pivot — the body of mature believers within a national entity — functions as the conduit through which blessing by association flows to the nation as a whole. Job 5:10 describes rain on the earth and water flowing over the fields as expressions of economic prosperity imputed by the integrity of God to a nation where a functioning pivot exists. When the pivot is absent or reduced, these blessings are withdrawn, and the five cycles of discipline become the operative principle in national history.

The individual mature believer in any historical climate — even under tyranny, economic collapse, or military defeat — retains full access to his personal SG2 blessings. His particular blessings differ from those of every other believer, because capacity differs with each individual and the blessing is always proportionate to the capacity that doctrine has built. No published list exhausts the catalogue of what the justice of God has prepared for the mature believer; the only adequate description is Job 5:9's phrase: marvellous things without number.

Conclusions from Chapter Two Hundred Eighty-Three

1. All blessing from God is a real imputation: it consists of a content imputed and an antecedent home prepared to receive it. The fourth real imputation — divine blessing in time to the righteousness of God resident in the believer — is the most complex because it requires two prior judicial imputations to make it possible.

2. The two judicial imputations are the foundation of all blessing: the imputation of personal sins to Christ on the cross (judicial imputation one) and the imputation of divine righteousness to the believer at salvation (judicial imputation two). Because greater provision was made at salvation adjustment, the justice of God will not withhold the lesser provision of blessing in time and eternity from the mature believer.

3. The grace pipeline is encapsulated: the justice of God gives to the righteousness of God. Nothing from the human side — witnessing, prayer, service, sacrifice, tithing, or any commanded action — can penetrate this screen. Blessing is not a reward for human activity; it is the product of God giving to God. No attribute of God is compromised.

4. God has no favorites: if the justice of God were to favor one believer above another on any personal basis, the divine integrity would be compromised and no believer could receive blessing. The impeccability of divine integrity is the foundation of every believer's security and the guarantee that the grace pipeline operates with perfect fairness.

5. Logistical grace is not mature blessing: everything the justice of God provides between salvation and maturity — food, shelter, health, relationships, financial support — is logistical support designed to carry the believer to the point of maturity. It is genuine provision and not to be despised, but it does not constitute paragraph SG2 blessing, which is imputed only when the maturity barrier is cracked.

6. Capacity is a prerequisite for blessing: blessing is not a blessing unless the recipient has the capacity to enjoy it and derive maximum happiness from it. Capacity is built exclusively through the consistent intake of Bible doctrine over time. Without capacity, prosperity produces misery rather than happiness — the principle that there are no advantages to the advantages without the advantage.

7. Divine discipline cannot be circumvented: when a believer is under the administration of the justice of God in discipline, the discipline will continue until its purpose is accomplished. No volume of intercessory prayer, no human assistance, and no external circumstance can abbreviate it. The appropriate and only effective response is rebound — naming known sins to God (1 John 1:9) — which restores fellowship, recovers the filling of the Spirit, and restores momentum toward maturity.

8. Undeserved suffering is a category of mature blessing: both deserved suffering (divine discipline) and undeserved suffering (suffering for blessing) originate in the justice of God and are therefore both fair and right. Deserved suffering is designed to hurt until the believer rebounds; undeserved suffering does not hurt in the same way because the mature believer has the capacity to remain above it and to glorify God through it. This principle is the bridge to Romans 8:18–30.

9. The grace pipeline operates independently of historical conditions: whether the national entity is in prosperity or under historical adversity, the justice of God continues to impute blessing to the righteousness of God in the soul of the mature believer. No political regime, economic collapse, military defeat, or combination of adverse circumstances can interrupt that transmission. The mature believer's SG2 blessings are beyond the reach of any external power.

10. Job 5 provides Old Testament confirmation of the grace pipeline: the integrity of God as the exclusive source of blessing, the futility of human appeal or merit, the instability of prosperity without capacity, the purpose of divine discipline, and the principle of undeserved suffering as blessing — all are present in Job 5, establishing that these are not New Testament innovations but the consistent testimony of Scripture. Job 5:19 introduces the six troubles that directly anticipate the suffering-glory pattern of Romans 8:18–30.

Glossary

Glossary

Term Greek / Transliteration Definition
Real imputation An imputation in which the content being imputed has an antecedent affinity with its target or home. The justice of God executes the imputation, and the two factors — content and target — correspond to each other by design. Examples: human life to the soul; Adam's original sin to the old sin nature; eternal life to regeneration; divine blessing to imputed righteousness.
Judicial imputation An imputation in which there is no antecedent affinity between the content and its assigned target. The imputation is executed by a judicial act of God rather than by natural correspondence. The two judicial imputations foundational to salvation are: (1) personal sins imputed to Christ on the cross; (2) divine righteousness imputed to the believer at salvation.
Paragraph SG2 The sixth category in the sequence of divine provision: blessing from the justice of God imputed to the mature believer. It includes six sub-categories, the sixth of which is undeserved suffering as a vehicle of blessing. SG2 blessing is the exclusive product of maturity adjustment to the justice of God.
Grace pipeline The encapsulated channel through which divine blessing flows from the justice of God (the giving end) to the righteousness of God resident in the mature believer (the receiving end). The pipeline is sealed: no human effort, religious activity, or merit can penetrate it. Blessing flows exclusively because God gives to God without compromise of any divine attribute.
Logistical grace God's provision of everything necessary for the believer's physical existence and continued spiritual advance between salvation and maturity. Logistical grace includes food, shelter, clothing, health, relationships, and all resources needed to sustain momentum toward the maturity barrier. It is distinguished from paragraph SG2 blessing in that it is provision for the journey rather than the blessing imputed at the destination.
Maturity barrier The threshold of spiritual maturity reached through consistent, sustained intake of Bible doctrine over time. When the edifice complex is constructed and maximum doctrine is resident in the soul, the maturity barrier is cracked. At this point, the righteousness of God demands blessing from the justice of God, and the justice of God executes that demand, imputing SG2 blessing to the mature believer.
Faith-rest The technique of taking adversity, pressure, or testing off oneself and imposing it upon God by means of claiming specific doctrinal promises. Faith-rest transfers the burden of impossible circumstances to the One who is capable of handling them, freeing the believer to maintain spiritual momentum rather than collapsing under pressure.
Undeserved suffering Suffering administered by the justice of God to the mature believer not as discipline but as a vehicle of blessing. Unlike deserved suffering, which is designed to hurt until the believer rebounds, undeserved suffering is borne by one who has the capacity to remain above it and to glorify God through it. It constitutes the sixth sub-category of paragraph SG2 and is the subject of Romans 8:18–30.
Pivot The body of mature believers within a national entity whose adjustment to the justice of God sustains divine blessing on that nation. The pivot is the mechanism of blessing by association: a nation benefits from the presence of mature believers even when the majority of its population is maladjusted to the justice of God. A diminished pivot exposes the nation to the five cycles of discipline.
Rebound 1 ιωαννου 1:9 1 John 1:9 The adjustment by which a believer out of fellowship with God restores that fellowship: naming known sins to God. Rebound is instantaneous, non-meritorious, and may be repeated as often as necessary. It is the mechanism of recovery from carnality and the prerequisite for continued advance toward maturity.
asah עָשָָה asah — to make, to manufacture Hebrew verb denoting the making of something from existing materials, as distinct from creation out of nothing. Used in Job 5:9 of the God who manufactures great and unsearchable things — specifically, blessing manufactured from the existing material of divine integrity itself, imputed to the mature believer without compromise of any divine attribute.

Chapter Two Hundred Eighty-Four

Romans 8:6–7 · Job 5:19–27 · Prosperity, Dying Grace, and the Hostility of the Old Sin Nature

Romans 8:6 “For to set the mind on the flesh is death, but to set the mind on the Spirit is life and peace.” (ESV)

Corrected translation: Consequently, the thought pattern of the flesh — the old sin nature — is death; but the thought pattern of the Spirit is capacity for life and prosperity.

Romans 8:7 “For the mind that is set on the flesh is hostile to God, for it does not submit to God's law; indeed, it cannot.” (ESV)

Corrected translation: Because the thought pattern of the flesh — the old sin nature — is hostile toward God.

Romans 8:6–7 stands at the center of the apostle's argument concerning the two opposing thought patterns available to the believer in the Church Age: the thought pattern of the old sin nature, which issues in spiritual death and hostility toward God, and the thought pattern of the Spirit, which issues in capacity for life and prosperity. To establish the content of that prosperity, the chapter draws on Job 5:19–27, one of the Old Testament's most concentrated expositions of the blessings that flow to the mature believer through maximum adjustment to the justice of God. The present chapter completes the exegesis of Job 5:19–27 and returns to Romans 8:7 to examine the nature and mechanism of reversionism as hostility toward God.

I. The Grace Pipeline and the Two Judicial Imputations

The organizing framework of Romans beginning at chapter 3 is the grace pipeline. On the originating end of this pipeline stands the justice of God; on the receiving end stands the righteousness of God. The justice of God is the believer's actual point of contact with God — not the love of God, which is communicated through anthropopathisms that have often misled casual students of Scripture. Justice is both the source of cursing and the source of blessing, and blessing that flows from divine justice is secure, permanent, and categorically superior to anything attainable by human effort.

The grace pipeline opens twice in the believer's experience. The first opening occurs at salvation, when thirty-four of the thirty-six things received at the moment of faith in Christ flow through this pipeline. The second opening occurs when the believer cracks the maturity barrier through the sustained daily function of the Grace Apparatus for Perception (GAP). It is this second opening — and the prosperity it releases — that is the subject of Romans 8 and the extended Job passage under study.

Two judicial imputations are required before the real imputation of divine blessing becomes possible. A judicial imputation has only one factor: what is being imputed. It is always imputed to what is not antecedently its own — there is no affinity between the imputed item and its recipient. A real imputation, by contrast, has two factors: what is being imputed and a divinely prepared home or target for that imputation, between which there is an inherent affinity.

A. The First Judicial Imputation: Sins Imputed to Christ at the Cross

At the cross, all personal sins of the entire human race were accumulated and imputed to the Lord Jesus Christ. This is a judicial imputation. There was no affinity between the personal sins of humanity and the impeccable God-man on the cross; these sins were not antecedently his own. Because the justice of God judged every one of these sins at that moment, eternal salvation is available to the entire world. This is the basis of the gospel: whoever believes in Christ shall not perish but have everlasting life.

It is important to note that no personal sin has ever been imputed for condemnation to any member of the human race. Only one sin serves as the basis of condemnation: Adam's original sin in the Garden. There is an affinity between Adam's original sin and the old sin nature, since Adam's original sin originated that nature. Accordingly, Adam's original sin is imputed to the genetically formed old sin nature at the moment of physical birth — a real imputation. This frees all personal sins for the judicial imputation to Christ.

B. The Second Judicial Imputation: Divine Righteousness Imputed at Salvation

At the moment of saving faith, God's perfect righteousness is imputed to the new believer. This also is a judicial imputation: divine righteousness is not antecedently the believer's own, and there is no inherent affinity between the perfect righteousness of God and any fallen member of the human race. The purpose of this imputation is to create a divinely prepared home — a target — for the real imputation of divine blessing at maturity. The receipt of God's righteousness at salvation is what the Scriptures call justification: the believer is declared qualified for blessing.

C. The Real Imputation of Divine Blessing at Maturity

When the believer cracks the maturity barrier, the justice of God executes what the righteousness of God demands: the real imputation of the six categories of supergrace blessing (paragraph SG2). These blessings flow through the grace pipeline to the believer's imputed divine righteousness as their divinely prepared home. Between divine blessing and divine righteousness there is a true affinity — both originate in the integrity of God.

The pattern of imputations across the believer's experience may be summarized as follows: at physical birth, human life is imputed to the soul (real imputation — affinity between life and soul) and Adam's original sin is imputed to the old sin nature (real imputation — affinity between Adam's sin and the sin nature). At regeneration, eternal life is imputed to the new birth prepared by the Holy Spirit (real imputation — affinity between eternal life and regeneration). At salvation adjustment, divine righteousness is imputed judicially to the believer with no antecedent affinity. At maturity adjustment, divine blessing is imputed really to the divinely prepared home of God's righteousness. The two judicial imputations — sins to Christ, righteousness to the believer — are the necessary preconditions for the real imputation of blessing in time. Blessing which belongs to the mature believer is categorically greater than what Adam and the woman possessed in the pristine perfection of the Garden of Eden.

Between salvation and the cracking of the maturity barrier, the believer exists under logistical grace. Logistical grace is the divine support system that keeps the believer alive and functional until maturity is reached: the provision of a right pastor, doctrinal teaching, the ministry of the Holy Spirit, and all physical necessities — food, shelter, clothing, transportation. These provisions, however excellent in quality, cannot be classified in the same category as the blessings released at maturity. They do not glorify God in the same way; they serve the purpose of sustaining life and pointing toward greater things to come.

II. Job 5:19–27: The Six Categories of SG2 Blessing

Job 5:19–27 is one of the most concentrated Old Testament expositions of the prosperity belonging to the mature believer. The passage is addressed specifically to the believer who has reached maximum adjustment to the justice of God. Each verse develops a dimension of the sixth category of SG2 blessing: undeserved suffering transformed into great blessing.

A. Verse 19: Deliverance in Six and Seven Troubles

Job 5:19 “He will deliver you from six troubles; in seven no evil shall touch you.” (ESV)

Corrected translation: In six troubles he will deliver you; furthermore, in seven evil will not touch you.

The verb rendered deliver is the Hiphil imperfect of natsal (נָצַל), to snatch from danger — used of rescuing a drowning person or delivering a soldier trapped and about to be overrun. The idiom six troubles … in seven is a graduated numerical formula expressing completeness: across the full range of adversity, God's deliverance is operative. The second clause employs the verb naga (נָגַע), to touch or to interfere. Evil — as the source of systemic disorder in human experience — will not interfere with the blessings that belong to the mature believer. The four categories of evil addressed in the following verses are economic, military, social, and dying disaster.

B. Verse 20: Economic and Military Disaster

Job 5:20 “In famine he will redeem you from death, and in war from the power of the sword.” (ESV)

Corrected translation: In famine he will redeem you from death; in war, from the power of the sword.

The verb padah (פָּדָה) — to redeem, to provide the means of preservation — governs the first clause. The promise is not that famine will not occur, but that the mature believer will be preserved through it. God is the active agent of preservation; human preparations, however prudent in themselves, are not the ultimate source of deliverance. The principle of Elijah at the Wadi Cherith is paradigmatic: having fled with nothing, God supplied his provision directly. The second clause addresses military disaster — the sword as the instrument of violent death in battle. The professional soldier whose integrity is grounded in maturity adjustment to the justice of God is sustained through military catastrophe in a way that military skill alone cannot secure.

C. Verse 21: Social Disaster and the Fear of Violent Death

Job 5:21 “You shall be hidden from the lash of the tongue, and shall not fear destruction when it comes.” (ESV)

Corrected translation: You will be hidden from the scourge of the tongue; neither will you be afraid of destruction when it comes.

The verb chaba (חָבָא), Niphal imperfect, means to be hidden or preserved from something sociologically destructive. The scourge of the tongue — gossip, maligning, judging, false accusation — is the characteristic weapon of social decadence. In periods of national decline and self-righteousness, those who are on the right track become targets of ridicule and slander. The mature believer is shielded from the corrosive effects of this social evil through his relationship with the integrity of God.

The second clause introduces the noun shod (שֹׁד), violent death. Fear of violent death — whether in an accident, a crash, drowning, or armed attack — is one of the most universal destroyers of capacity for life. The verb yare (יָרֵא), Qal imperfect, establishes that such fear is eliminated by maturity adjustment. The believer who has cracked the maturity barrier knows that God governs the dying as well as the living, and that dying grace — the blessing available in the process of death itself — makes violent death a matter of divine provision rather than human dread.

D. Verse 22: Relaxed Laughter at Violent Death and Economic Depression

Job 5:22 “At destruction and famine you shall laugh, and shall not fear the beasts of the earth.” (ESV)

Corrected translation: You will laugh at violent death and economic depression; and from the wild animals of the earth you will have nothing to fear.

The Qal imperfect of sachaq (שָׂחַק) denotes not hysteria but the relaxed laughter of inner security — the capacity that comes when fear has been eliminated from the life by a total relationship with the integrity of God. This is not a superficial emotional response; it is the outward expression of maximum doctrine resident in the soul. The verse returns to the first and last of the four evils — violent death and economic disaster — as the categories most universally productive of fear. Wild animals, as instruments of violent death in the ancient world, represent the same class of threat that in subsequent centuries has been represented by other means of sudden and catastrophic death. The principle remains constant: the mature believer's security is grounded not in any human system of provision or self-protection but in the integrity of God.

E. Verse 23: Covenant with Weapons and Peace with the Animal Kingdom

Job 5:23 “For you shall be in league with the stones of the field, and the beasts of the field shall be at peace with you.” (ESV)

Corrected translation: For your covenant will be with the stones of the field, and the beasts of the field will be at peace with you.

The stones of the field at the time of writing referred to missiles used as weapons — projectiles delivered by slings and catapult mechanisms, the artillery of the ancient world. The promise is that no military weapon will destroy the mature believer until God's appointed time. The wild animals of the earth, as instruments of violent death, will likewise be at peace with such a believer. The underlying principle is absolute: no instrument of death can remove the mature believer from this life independently of the schedule of divine integrity. Only the justice of God transfers the believer from time to eternity, and only when the plan of God for that individual in time has been completed.

F. Verse 24: Dying Grace — the Tent in Prosperity

Job 5:24 “You shall know that your tent is in peace, and you shall inspect your fold and miss nothing.” (ESV)

Corrected translation: Therefore, you will know that your human body is in a state of prosperity; and you will visit your home and fear no loss.

The verb yada (יָדַע), Qal perfect, means to know through perception — the same cognitive mechanism employed in the Grace Apparatus for Perception. The perfect tense indicates completed action: this is already-acquired knowledge, doctrine resident in the soul. The tent or tabernacle is a standard Hebrew idiom for the human body as a temporary dwelling. The body of the mature believer is in shalom — prosperity — in the process of dying. Whether death is instantaneous or prolonged, the mature believer passes through the process under divine blessing, sustained by dying grace.

The second clause employs paqad (פָּקַד), to visit a place of pleasure — a verb of anticipation and enjoyment. Heaven is the home being visited; the word carries the connotation of a welcomed arrival. The absence of any loss of eternal blessing or reward confirms that the mature believer enters eternity with all that maximum adjustment to the justice of God has secured. This is one of the six categories of SG2 blessing: the blessing that comes through the dying process itself.

G. Verse 25: Blessing by Association for Those Left Behind

Job 5:25 “You shall know also that your offspring shall be many, and your descendants as the grass of the earth.” (ESV)

Corrected translation: Also, you will know that your seed will be many, your offspring like young shoots of the field.

The word for seed functions idiomatically for prosperity extended to loved ones left behind after the mature believer's death. The believer who has cracked the maturity barrier before dying has left the only truly secure legacy: blessing by association flowing from the integrity of God to those connected with him. No insurance policy or accumulated estate constitutes a comparable provision. The agricultural imagery — offspring like young shoots of the field — conveys abundance and vitality as the natural consequence of proximity to a life built on divine integrity.

H. Verse 26: Full Age — Perfect Timing in Death

Job 5:26 “You shall come to your grave in ripe old age, like a sheaf gathered up in its season.” (ESV)

Corrected translation: You will come to the grave in a full age, like a shock of corn in its season.

The Qal imperfect of bo (בּוֹא) — to arrive, to come — governs the verse. The expression full age does not mean old age but the peak of a person's divinely appointed time: the moment at which the integrity of God determines that the plan of God for that individual in time has been completed. Full age may be thirteen, thirty-three, forty-five, or eighty-five — the integer is irrelevant. The expert determines when the harvest is ready, and God is the expert. The agricultural analogy of corn gathered in its season captures both the precision and the benevolence of the divine timing. The soul's separation from the body at death corresponds to the grain's separation from the stalk: the right moment, executed by the right hand. Neither the believer nor any observer has the standing to question the integrity of God regarding the timing of death, whether early or late by human reckoning.

I. Verse 27: The Command to Hear and Internalize

Job 5:27 “Behold, this we have searched out; it is true. Hear, and know it for your good.” (ESV)

Corrected translation: We have investigated this. This is the substance of it. Hear it. Know it for yourself.

The verb chaqar (חָקַר), Qal perfect, means a thorough investigation — exegetical research completed and summarized. Two imperatives follow: shama (שָׁמַע), Qal imperative — hear it, receive it; and yada (יָדַע), Qal imperative — know it, make it your own personal property. The progression is deliberate: investigation produces doctrine; hearing receives it; knowing internalizes it as epignosis — full, exact perception resident in the soul. This is the mechanism by which the promises of Job 5:19–26 become operational in the believer's experience.

III. Romans 8:6 Revisited: Capacity for Life and Prosperity

Returning now to Romans 8:6, the passage's corrected translation reads: Consequently, the thought pattern of the old sin nature is death; but the thought pattern of the Spirit — Bible doctrine in the power of the Holy Spirit — is capacity for life and prosperity. The six categories of SG2 blessing established in the Job passage are precisely the content of this prosperity: deliverance from economic disaster, military disaster, social disaster, violent death, and the extension of blessing by association to those who survive the mature believer. A sixth category is supplied by Romans 8:18: undeserved suffering as great blessing.

The word translated prosperity corresponds to the Greek noun eirēnē (εἰρήνη) — peace in the sense of prosperous well-being, the condition of one who is in right relationship with God through the justice-righteousness nexus of the grace pipeline. The believer who has cracked the maturity barrier through the daily function of GAP possesses this condition regardless of external circumstances. The believer who is dominated by the old sin nature — whether through carnality or reversionism — has no access to it, because his thought pattern is oriented away from the things of the Spirit.

The contrast between the two thought patterns in verse 6 is not merely behavioral but ontological: the thought pattern of the old sin nature is death — the condition of spiritual dysfunction, separation from the operational blessings of the grace pipeline, and ultimately the sin unto death — while the thought pattern of the Spirit is life and prosperity in the full SG2 sense. The believer who rejects or neglects Bible doctrine invariably dies spiritually in this functional sense, because the thought pattern of the old sin nature, left uncontested by doctrine, inevitably dominates the right lobe.

IV. Romans 8:7: The Hostility of the Reversionistic Thought Pattern

Romans 8:7 “For the mind that is set on the flesh is hostile to God, for it does not submit to God's law; indeed, it cannot.” (ESV)

Corrected translation: Because the thought pattern of the flesh — the old sin nature — is hostile toward God.

The verse opens with the causal conjunction dioti (διότι) — because — which provides the reason for the death announced in verse 6. The subject is phronēma (φρόνημα), thought pattern, modified by the possessive genitive of sarx (σάρξ) — the old sin nature. The predicate nominative is echthra (ἔχθρα), enmity or hostility, followed by the directional preposition eis (εἰς) plus the accusative of theos (θεός). The hostility is directed toward God — not a general religious indifference but an active antagonism toward the integrity of God, the plan of God, and the policy of God for the Church Age believer.

A. The Mechanism of Enmity: The Two Roads

The old sin nature generates enmity toward God through two distinct roads. The first is the road of sin without rebound: the believer who sins and fails to name that sin to God (1 John 1:9) remains in a state of carnality, cut off from the filling of the Holy Spirit and therefore from spiritual growth. The second road is the road of human good — religious and moral activity performed in the energy of the old sin nature rather than in the power of the Holy Spirit. Both roads lead to evil as a thought pattern and, sustained over time, to reversionism. Evil is the operating system of the old sin nature in the religious and moralistic mode; it is more dangerous than overt sin precisely because it presents itself as virtue while systematically excluding the integrity of God from the believer's life.

B. Carnality and Reversionism Distinguished

The carnal state and the reversionistic state overlap in their common character as hostility toward God, but they are distinguished by the complexity of their solution. Carnality — the state of a believer out of fellowship through known unconfessed sin — is resolved immediately and completely by rebound: naming the known sin to God, on the authority of 1 John 1:9, restores the filling of the Holy Spirit instantly. Reversionism — the sustained pattern of retrograde spiritual regression under the dominance of the old sin nature's trend toward moral and religious good — requires rebound plus the sustained intake of maximum doctrine to reverse. The carnal believer is a culprit; the reversionistic believer has become an enemy. Both are in a state of enmity toward God, but reversionism represents the more entrenched condition.

C. The Marriage Analogy: Positional Divorce from the Old Sin Nature

The apostle's argument in Romans 6–8 employs a marriage analogy to clarify the believer's relationship to the old sin nature. In the first marriage — the condition of every human being from physical birth — the old sin nature functions as husband, the human being as wife, and the Mosaic Law as the marriage counselor who reveals the dysfunction of the union. At salvation, the baptism of the Holy Spirit accomplishes a positional divorce through identification with Christ.

Retroactive positional truth identifies the believer with Christ in his spiritual death — the rejection of the old sin nature's policy of good and evil — and with Christ in his physical death, which is separation from the old sin nature. Identification with Christ in his burial constitutes the actual positional divorce: the old sin nature is dead to the believer, and the believer is dead to the old sin nature, in the same way that former spouses are dead to each other after divorce, even while both remain physically alive.

Current positional truth then identifies the believer with Christ in his resurrection and session at the right hand of the Father. The second marriage has Christ as husband, the believer as wife, and the Holy Spirit as the marriage counselor. In this second marriage there can be only one culprit, because Christ and the Holy Spirit are both perfect: the culprit is the believer who refuses to use rebound and neglects the intake of doctrine. The old sin nature, though positionally dead, remains experientially active within the body and continues to solicit the believer's return — precisely the enmity described in Romans 8:7. The resolution is experiential sanctification: the filling of the Holy Spirit plus maximum doctrine resident in the soul, producing maturity adjustment to the justice of God.

V. The Corrected Translation of Romans 8:1–7

The following corrected translation represents the progress made through this section of Romans 8:

Now therefore there is no judgment to those who are in Christ Jesus. For the principle of the Spirit — that is, the ministry of the Holy Spirit at salvation — who is the source of eternal life, has set you free in Christ Jesus from the principle of the sin nature and resultant spiritual death. For what was impossible from the law, because it was weak through the flesh, God accomplished by sending His own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh and as a sin offering: He judged the sin nature in the flesh. In order that the legal requirement of the law might be fulfilled in us who keep walking not according to the old sin nature but according to the Spirit. For those believers who are dominated by the old sin nature keep thinking about the things of the old sin nature. Those believers who are dominated by the Holy Spirit keep thinking about the things of the Spirit — that is, Bible doctrine. Consequently, the thought pattern of the old sin nature is death; but the thought pattern of the Spirit is capacity for life and prosperity. Because the thought pattern of the flesh — the old sin nature — is hostile toward God.

Conclusions from Chapter Two Hundred Eighty-Four

1. The grace pipeline originates in the justice of God and terminates in the righteousness of God. The believer's point of contact with God is justice, not love. All divine blessing — both at salvation and at maturity — flows through this pipeline. Anthropopathisms describing the love of God should not be read as identifying love as the mechanism of blessing; justice is the mechanism.

2. Two judicial imputations are the necessary precondition for every real imputation of divine blessing. Judicial imputation number one: all personal sins imputed to Christ at the cross, judged by divine justice. Judicial imputation number two: God's perfect righteousness imputed to the believer at salvation, creating the divinely prepared home for blessing. Real imputation of SG2 blessing at maturity is the result of both judicial imputations combined.

3. Logistical grace sustains the believer between salvation and the maturity barrier; it is not SG2 blessing. Food, shelter, transportation, friendship, and other provisions during this period are real and valuable, but they do not glorify God in the same category as the blessings released at maturity. They are the means of sustaining life until the greater blessings can be received.

4. Job 5:19–27 identifies four categories of disaster that cannot touch the mature believer: economic, military, social, and violent death. Each category is addressed by a specific Hebrew verb expressing God's active intervention: natsal (deliverance), padah (redemption), chaba (concealment), and yare negated (elimination of fear). The mature believer is not promised the absence of these disasters but the presence of divine blessing through them.

5. Full age is not old age but the precise moment at which the integrity of God determines that the believer's plan in time is complete. Death at any age — infancy, youth, or advanced years — can constitute full age in the divine reckoning. The agricultural analogy of corn gathered in its season establishes that God alone determines the harvest moment. The appropriate response to early or unexpected death is not bitterness or questioning of divine integrity but confidence that God knows exactly what he is doing.

6. Dying grace is a positive blessing, not a catastrophe. The mature believer passes from time to eternity across what may be described as a high golden bridge — whether the passage is instantaneous or prolonged, divine blessing is operative every moment of the transition. The human body of the mature believer is in a state of prosperity in death. There is no basis for the survivor's horror at violent or sudden death when the deceased was a mature believer.

7. Blessing by association extends SG2 prosperity to the loved ones of the mature believer after his death. The only secure legacy a believer can leave is the blessing by association that flows from the integrity of God to those connected with a life built on maximum doctrine. No financial instrument, accumulated estate, or material provision constitutes a comparable inheritance.

8. The thought pattern of the old sin nature is intrinsically hostile toward God. Romans 8:7 identifies this hostility as the causal ground for the spiritual death described in verse 6. The hostility is not incidental or occasional; it is the defining orientation of the old sin nature's thought pattern. Both carnality and reversionism are expressions of this enmity, differing in degree and in the complexity of their resolution but identical in kind.

9. The solution to enmity toward God is experiential sanctification: the filling of the Holy Spirit plus maximum doctrine resident in the soul. Carnality is resolved by rebound alone. Reversionism requires rebound plus sustained doctrine intake. In both cases, the operational mechanism is the Grace Apparatus for Perception (GAP) — hearing, receiving, and internalizing Bible doctrine under the enabling ministry of the Holy Spirit until the maturity barrier is cracked and full maturity adjustment to the justice of God is achieved.

10. Romans 8:18 supplies the sixth category of SG2 blessing: undeserved suffering as great blessing. The sufferings of the present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory that shall be revealed in us. This anticipates the extended argument of Romans 8:18 and following, where undeserved suffering — the pressures, disasters, and adversities that fall upon the mature believer specifically — is identified as a manifestation of divine blessing rather than divine abandonment.
